## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`list_orders` accepts a `limit` but no `offset`, so the order listing can return only its first page even though the title describes pagination; this should be fixed. The text of issue #12 was unavailable, so this review could not confirm what the issue requires.

## Changes
The pull request adds `paginate(items, limit, offset=0)` in `app/paging.py` and gives `list_orders` an optional `limit` that it passes to that helper after sorting. It adds one test for the limit in `tests/test_orders.py` and a new `tests/test_paging.py` covering offset, no limit, and negative arguments.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/orders.py:9 — correctness — Expose offset on list_orders so later pages are reachable — A caller that needs orders 3–4 of five cannot get them: `list_orders(orders, limit=2)` always returns the newest two, because `paginate(ordered, limit)` leaves `offset` at its default of 0 and `list_orders` has no parameter to set it. — The order listing serves only its first page, so the pagination the title describes is unavailable to callers. — Fix: Add `offset=0` to `list_orders`, pass it as `paginate(ordered, limit, offset)`, and extend `test_limit_caps_results` in `tests/test_orders.py` with a second-page case.

## Suggestions
- app/paging.py:12 — tests — Add a test for limit=0 — `paginate([1, 2, 3], limit=0)` returns `[]` because line 12 tests `limit is None` rather than truthiness, but no test in `tests/test_paging.py` or `tests/test_orders.py` passes `limit=0`. — A later change to `if not limit` would return every item for `limit=0` without failing a test.

## Not reviewed
- The text of issue #12, which the pull-request body closes, was not available in the repository or in `../pr.json`, so conformance to it was not checked.
